summary.headline: Gravita Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR1,475 crore and PAT 14% to INR106.39 crore, but lead volumes fell on Gulf supply disruption.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 42% YoY to INR1,475 crore, adjusted EBITDA rose 29% to INR145 crore (margin above 9.80%) and PAT rose 14% to INR106.39 crore. Total volumes grew only 4% YoY to 55,455 MT, and management said lead volumes declined YoY because Middle East war logistics disrupted scrap imports (15-20% of imports come via the Gulf). The copper subsidiary (Rashtriya Metal Industries) ran at 50% utilisation and contributed INR376 crore revenue. Management said it is compensating lost lead volume with better realisations and expects lead EBITDA margins to hold next quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA per ton: lead / aluminium / plastic / copper

financial_highlights.value: INR47 crore (INR35 crore operational, INR13 crore non-operational)

financial_highlights.change: higher on copper inventory and goods in transit

segments.name: Lead (Mundra, Phagi, Chittoor)
segments.commentary: Volumes declined YoY on Gulf supply disruption; Mundra utilisation about 50% and Jaipur lead about 45% after expansion. Management expects similar lead EBITDA margins next quarter.

segments.name: Copper (Rashtriya Metal Industries subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Ran at 50% utilisation, INR376 crore revenue, EBITDA about INR55,151/MT. Target to reach about 60% utilisation by end FY27 and double capacity to about 60,000 MT per annum in three years.

segments.name: Aluminium and plastic
segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton of INR25,175 (aluminium) and INR10,197 (plastic) in Q1 were boosted by price gains; sustainable plastic EBITDA guided at INR10-12/kg and aluminium at INR15-17/kg when overseas operations run.

capex_capacity: Total installed capacity 4.97 lakh MT per annum; on track to exceed 8 lakh MT per annum by FY29.

Phagi (Jaipur) lead expansion of 40,500 MTPA commissioned in Q1 for about INR30 crore from internal accruals; plant total now 75,819 MTPA. Management guided about INR50 crore additional revenue per month at 70% utilisation, but ramp-up is awaiting scrap normalisation, expected by end FY27.
Copper recycling facility of 29,400 MTPA in Gujarat at about INR160 crore, on track for commissioning within 12 months, funded by internal accruals.
Total capex of INR1,680 crore through FY29: INR850 crore for existing businesses, balance for lithium-ion, copper and steel verticals.
Kathua unit operations to be consolidated into the Jaipur facility. Rubber capacity (Eastern Europe) put on hold; copper expansion fast-tracked in that plant's space.
demand_pricing: Lead LME brand listing achieved for Mundra-produced lead under GRAVITA M brand; lead now deliverable to LME-approved warehouses in addition to MCX.
Copper EBITDA guided at around INR55,000/MT sustainable, rising to INR60,000 by end FY27 and INR65,000-75,000 over 2-3 years; copper hedged 100% so commodity upside is limited.
Aluminium ADC12 inclusion on MCX still pending with the exchange; management hopes for it within this year.
Domestic sourcing about 35% for India plants; scrap yard network rose from 33% to about 39%+ over three quarters.
Group capacity utilisation about 52% in Q1 across the expanded Jaipur and Mundra capacity; target about 70% sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lead volumes decline YoY and what is the FY27 volume guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to Gulf supply chain disruption, which blocks 15-20% of imports. Division-wise volume guidance was declined; management expects lower quarter-to-quarter volume growth near term, with long-term growth in line with Vision 2030.

qa_highlights.question: When will copper utilisation reach 100%, and why is copper EBITDA margin below last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Debottlenecking will run through FY27, with bottleneck removal by year-end; major utilisation gains expected then. Last year's copper EBITDA included copper price gains; with 100% hedging, sustainable margin is about INR55,000/MT, rising to INR65,000-70,000 over 2-2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and working capital cycle at Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR150 crore and working capital cycle about 95 days, raised by copper inventory build and goods in transit.

qa_highlights.question: What is utilisation of the new lead capacity at Mundra and Phagi?
qa_highlights.answer: Mundra utilisation about 50% including February expansion; Jaipur lead about 45%; group about 52%. Sustainable utilisation about 70% depends on scrap availability.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new procurement network in developed economies incremental cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said own yards in the US would cut procurement cost versus buying through agents, and would be used for copper, lead, aluminium and plastic.

qa_highlights.question: What is ROCE and the other income split?
qa_highlights.answer: ROCE about 20% currently including copper, expected to rise towards 25% over about three years. Other income INR47 crore: INR35 crore operational, INR13 crore non-operational.

risks_watch: Gulf logistics disruption continues to hold back scrap imports; management expects some Q2 impact.
Lead volume decline and under-utilised new lead capacity (Mundra about 50%, Jaipur about 45%).
Copper utilisation at 50% with EBITDA per ton of INR55,151, below the INR65,000+ levels the company referenced earlier; working capital rising to about 95 days.
ROCE about 20% is below the company's historical levels; management targets 25%+ in about 2.5-3 years.
Pending MCX aluminium (ADC12) inclusion timing is outside company control.
guidance_outlook: Lead EBITDA margins expected to hold similar next quarter despite top-line pressure.
Copper EBITDA about INR55,000/MT sustainable, about INR60,000 by end FY27, INR65,000-75,000 over 2-3 years.
Copper utilisation about 60% plus by end FY27; capacity to about 60,000 MTPA in three years.
Management reiterated PAT CAGR target of 25-30% for FY27 and the next 4-5 years; 8 lakh MT capacity by FY29.
Phagi lead expansion to add about INR50 crore revenue per month at 70% utilisation, contingent on scrap normalisation by year-end.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and diversification but cautious on near-term volumes; management repeatedly attributed lead shortfalls to Gulf logistics disruption and gave few division-wise volume numbers. Answers were most specific on margins, EBITDA per ton and capex timelines.
key_quotes: So although there may be some impact in terms of top line growth, but we are expecting similar kind of bottom line or EBITDA margins in the next quarter also, as far as lead is concerned.

So it's extremely difficult to talk about on a division -wise volume growth, especially in a very short-term period because, as I mentioned, there is some disruption, which is still not back to normal.
We don't sell our product on LME. We've not sold any product on LME because it's not a very profitable proposition.

adds.what: Phagi (Jaipur) lead expansion of 40,500 MTPA, commissioned in Q1 (plant total 75,819 MTPA)
Copper recycling facility of 29,400 MTPA in Gujarat

growth.why: Management reiterated 25-30% PAT CAGR and 8 lakh MTPA capacity by FY29, with the Phagi expansion commissioned and copper capacity doubling planned in 3 years; however, lead volumes fell on Gulf scrap disruption, the Phagi ramp awaits scrap normalisation by end FY27, and group utilisation is only about 52%, so backing is partial.
